notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.18_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.18.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.18.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Changed

- **A first launch that asks two questions instead of six.** The welcome screen
  showed a QR code of a key nobody had heard of yet, a username box, a relay
  chooser, a recovery phrase to write down and a paragraph about pairing — all
  at once, to somebody who had opened the app fifteen seconds ago.

  It now asks the only two things that decide what happens next: pick a name
  and create an account, or — if you already have one somewhere — paste the
  code from that device. The second is a real link, the same exchange account
  settings offers, so a new device arrives with the name, the friends and the
  servers already on it rather than as a stranger who has to be told everything
  again. It was previously reachable only by finding it in settings, which is a
  strange thing to ask of somebody whose settings are empty.

  Everything else is under **Advanced** at the foot: your key and its QR code,
  the recovery phrase, restoring from one, and which relay to use. All still
  one click away, none of it in the way.

### Fixed

- **Linking an account now brings its name and picture too.** The account
  moved, its servers moved, its friends moved — and the profile stayed behind,
  because the profile is not part of the account. It is a file beside the key,
  held per device. So the phone became the right person under whatever name
  that phone had been calling itself, and one human showed up under two names
  depending which of their devices you were looking at.

  The name and the picture now travel in the same frame as the account, and are
  taken on before it is adopted — adopting writes an entry into every server,
  and those should say the name the account already goes by rather than the old
  one with a correction arriving behind it. The picture is fetched from the
  device that just handed the account over, because that device demonstrably
  has it and is demonstrably reachable; if it does not arrive in ten seconds
  the hash is recorded anyway and the picture draws when it does.

- **Your profile is reachable without being in a server.** The row with your
  picture, name, status and microphone lived at the foot of the channel list,
  and the channel list only exists when a server is open — so a device that had
  joined nothing, or anyone simply looking at their friends, had no profile row
  and no way to reach the panel behind it. It sits at the foot of the friends
  list as well now.
